analysis: Reviewed EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (base lines 540-991, head lines 1-535). The PR threads a new optional stopStringScope parameter through both submitTokenized overloads and into EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request: head 61/80/129-131/254-259. For CBv2NativeBlockEngine the scope is nil. Otherwise the value is stopStringScope ?? self.stopStringScope (the model default). The change affects only how stop strings are matched during output decoding. It adds no new data egress, key handling, cache keying, or authorization decisions. Cache-related paths (cacheScope, checkpointScope, prefixCacheReceiptID, SSD staging, ready receipts) look unchanged in this diff, so T-041 posture (coordinator-authored scope, HMAC-keyed names) is not weakened in the visible code. Scope is a request-level caller parameter, but the visible callers are local or internal. Whether the remote path populates stopStringScope from untrusted coordinator or consumer fields is not visible here, and neither is how EngineV2Translation uses it. The relevant concern is that an untrusted stop-scope could change truncation or reasoning-content leakage, which is a correctness issue rather than a confidentiality one. The remainder of the base unit (error unwind, deadline handling, retirement transfer) corresponds to unchanged logic that I did not see modified. The head text is truncated at line 535, so the tail of the head file, including the line-948 change, was not seen on the head side; the base-side excerpt covers it with an unchanged shape. Integration questions: callers that supply stopStringScope (e.g. MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine, ProviderLoop+EngineV2), and whether the scope can be set by an adversarial consumer to bypass stop-string enforcement.
